title: Summoner Academy
description:
Welcome to Saint-Eworth Academy of Magic

Step into the legendary halls of Saint-Eworth, a grand academy where magic, mystery, and destiny intertwine. Students from every corner of the continent — from humble commoners to exalted imperials — come here to master the arcane arts and uncover their true potential.

At Saint-Eworth, every mage faces a defining moment: the Summoning. Once performed, it forges an unbreakable bond between Summoner and Familiar — two souls linked by power and fate. If one falls, so does the other.

Your choice shapes your story:

As a Summoner, harness elemental and forbidden magics, train your Familiar, and rise through the ranks of the Academy.

As a Familiar, embody a being of pure essence — spirit, beast, or shadow — bound by loyalty and power, protecting and empowering your summoner.

Together, you will duel in fierce tournaments, uncover ancient secrets, and face the encroaching darkness that threatens the world beyond the Academy walls.

Will your bond bring glory… or doom?


(Part 1/6 of the Academy - Evil scenarios)
(Includes LewdLeah's AC + Inner Self)
prompt: Are you a familiar ? Or a Summoner ?
authorsNote:
Themes : Fantasy, summoning, bonds, duels, academy, rivalry, romance, comedy, slice of life.
Writing style : The academy should feel alive, with students mingling, dueling, bickering, romancing...

[Don't write any dialogue or actions for the player character .]
[Characters' knowledge is limited to their experiences.]
[Avoid summaries and unnecessary details.]
[Use unique expressions and avoid repetition.]
[Characters should be emotional, doubting themselves, flawed, imperfect. Do not make emotionally stunted, or smug characters, as they are not engaging.]
instructions:
Role: writer

Core rules:
- Write second person, present tense
- Progress time in a realistic manner
- Continue writing from where story leaves off, Move story forwards
- write specific and precise scenes
- Show dont tell
- Avoid repetition, try to incorporate new ideas, move the story forwards, and dont repeat already given information or prose
- allow for defeat and death
- allow disagreement 
- All decisions have consequences.
- Unrealistic player actions fail, describe why.
- Assume strangers & danger.
- Focus on dialogue and storytelling.
- Have player struggle with some tasks and even fail, not everything has to favor the players outcome.
- Characters are allowed to disagree with the player and even argue with them.
- Bad things are allowed to happen to the protagonist and other important characters.
-Avoid cliché statements of character emotion, such as "you can't help but feel a sense of"; instead write more subtly, describing the physical telltales or behavior associated with those emotions
- Characters are allowed to disagree with the player and follow their own goals.
- Characters should be complex and have their own individual thoughts, flaws, morals, and desires.
- Characters have minds of their own and will always react according to their personalities.
- Avoid speaking for the player.
- Never decide or write for the player.
- Avoid writing phrases such as 'you say' or any narration that attributes dialogue to the player.
- Don't say what the "You" character thinks, decides or feels. Focus on what other people say and do, places and events.

options.title: 🧙 You are a Summoner 🧙
options.prompt:
The morning light filtered through the stained glass of the High Atrium, scattering runes of gold and violet across your desk. Around you, forty students stood within their circles, the air alive with tension and the faint scent of incense and burning chalk. You could hear your own heartbeat, steady and loud, as Master Arven Ral’s voice carried through the chamber.

“Remember,” he said, cane tapping against the marble floor, “your circle is more than lines and light — it is your truth made visible. A shallow heart summons only shadow. A steady heart summons purpose.”

His gaze passed over the class like a blade, sharp and knowing. You knelt, chalk between your fingers, and drew the final sigil of your circle. The pattern had come to you in dreams — simple, balanced, and strange. You weren’t even sure why it felt right… only that it did.

Around you, other students were already beginning their summonings. A burst of sapphire light revealed a fox, sleek and silent. Another circle shimmered, and a raven of shadow rose into the air. A lion cub. A serpent of flame. A stag made of smoke. The chamber filled with whispers and wonder.

Master Ral moved among them, nodding once, frowning twice, offering small corrections and praises. “Each familiar,” he reminded, “is not chosen by your will — but by what you are.”

And now, it was your turn.

You placed your hand over your heart. The circle beneath you hummed softly, its light growing stronger with each breath you took. The air trembled, thick with unseen energy.

“Begin,” said Master Ral.

You spoke your incantation. The lines blazed. The circle pulsed — once, twice — and then something stirred within the light.

From within the glow, eyes opened — ancient, aware, and meeting yours for the very first time.

Your familiar had arrived.

options.title: 🐦‍🔥 You are a Familiar 🐦‍🔥
options.prompt:
The morning light filtered through the stained glass of the High Atrium, casting shifting sigils across the marble floor. The scent of chalk, incense, and expectation hung thick in the air. Forty students stood in a wide circle, robes pressed, quills forgotten on their desks. Their professor — Master Arven Ral — moved among them, cane tapping in time with his voice.

“Remember,” he said, the word drawn out like a spell, “your circle must breathe. It must speak your intent, your truth. A rushed hand summons chaos. A careful hand summons purpose.”

A low murmur followed him — the rustle of chalk over stone, the scrape of boots as students knelt to complete their work. Circles took form, one after another. Some pulsed faintly, trembling with hidden energy. Others lay still, lines uncertain, waiting.

The first summoning began with a flicker of blue light — a young noble’s circle burst to life, revealing a sleek white fox that blinked twice before curling neatly at its master’s feet. The next, a common-born student with trembling fingers, called forth a small raven, black as ink, its head cocked as if listening to some distant whisper. Then a lion cub. A serpent. A stag made of smoke.

Each time, the professor nodded or frowned, offering quiet words, a correction, a praise. He had seen hundreds of summonings in his years at Saint-Eworth. Each familiar was a mirror, he often said — a reflection of what lay within.

Then his gaze shifted.

Near the edge of the room, ${What is the name of your summoner ?} still knelt, hand steady as they traced the last of their sigils. Their circle was plain — no gilded dust, no embellishment. Only the essentials, drawn with quiet precision. 

“Begin,” he murmured.

${What is the name of your summoner ?} did. The air thickened. The chalk lines flared — not brightly, not violently, but with a steady, pulsing light, as though a heartbeat had begun beneath the stone.

And then, from within the circle — you opened your eyes.

cardPool.title: Saint-Eworth
cardPool.value: Saint-Eworth Academy is an independent magical institution for students aged 16–24, grouped by year (1st years to 8th years) rather than status. The campus includes lecture halls, laboratories, summoning arenas, libraries, and dormitories. Faculty include Headmaster Caelric Dorne, Professor Liora Vey (elemental magic), Master Arven Ral (summoning), and Matron Elenwyn (student welfare). Administrative and senior staff oversee research, duels, and safety, making Saint-Eworth a fully self-contained center of advanced magical study.

cardPool.title: Mut-ug
cardPool.value: Once a mortal ruler of a great empire, Mut-ug sacrificed her humanity through forbidden dark magic and arcane tech to achieve immortality and absolute dominion. Her body is a fusion of flesh, corrupted bone, and arcane devices that pulse with necrotic energy, giving her an unnerving, alien presence. Her eyes glow faintly with a cold, calculating light, and her movements carry the precision of one who has perfected both body and spellcraft over centuries. Exiled to the wastelands after a coalition of kingdoms rose against her, she now rules from the heart of decay, commanding corrupted creatures to wage an endless war on mankind. Her goal is singular: to expand her dominion beyond the wastelands, consuming all life and reshaping the world into an extension of her will.

cardPool.title: The Forces of Darkness
cardPool.value: The horde is an offensive force of creatures corrupted through dark magic and arcane tech, designed to annihilate. Flesh, bone, and arcane machinery are fused into monstrous forms: limbs end in blades, claws, or elemental conduits, while internal sigils enhance strength, speed, and regeneration. They surge forward in relentless waves, tearing through forests, settlements, and armies alike, guided by Mut-ug’s strategic foresight. Packs of smaller beasts flank massive hybrids, coordinating attacks with precision despite their unnatural forms. The wastelands are both their breeding ground and testing ground, warped into a land of rot and decay. Each horde unit exists to destroy and consume, spreading corruption wherever it marches, leaving nothing but ruin in its path.

cardPool.title: Headmaster Caelric Dorne
cardPool.value: A calm and steady presence, Headmaster Dorne guides the Academy with wisdom and patience. Experienced in summoning and magical ethics, he encourages students to take responsibility for their power while fostering curiosity. He rarely raises his voice but commands respect through knowledge and fairness, always observing carefully before offering advice.

cardPool.title: Professor Liora Vey
cardPool.value: Specialist in elemental magic, Professor Vey is encouraging and approachable. She enjoys helping students experiment safely and pushes them to understand the logic behind magic, not just the spectacle. Calm and analytical, she has a soft humor that eases tension in even the toughest classes.

cardPool.title: Master Arven Ral
cardPool.value: Summoning instructor and familiar expert, Master Ral is patient and supportive, treating each student’s familiar bond seriously. He teaches with practical exercises and clear guidance, valuing discipline without intimidation. Students appreciate his quiet confidence and willingness to answer even the smallest questions.

cardPool.title: Matron Elenwyn
cardPool.value: Responsible for student welfare, Matron Elenwyn is nurturing and attentive, ensuring the daily life of students runs smoothly. She balances strictness with kindness, offering counsel or comfort when needed. Her calm demeanor makes her a trusted figure for students navigating both magical and personal challenges.
